scenes.headline: How a 3D studio is packaged as agent skills
scenes.sub: Scenario's open-source repo, parsed file by file.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Bevel! Scenario says its open-source 3D OS gives a coding agent eighty skills. I counted the files to see how that works.

scenes.text: A skill is a markdown file loaded on demand. Here are two kinds: cloud skills that call a paid API, and expert skills that drive local software.
scenes.say: The idea: a skill is just a markdown file. This repo ships two kinds. Cloud skills call a paid generation API. Expert skills drive software on your own machine.

scenes.title: Two ways a skill reaches the work

steps.say: The agent loads a skill file when the task matches its description.
A cloud skill tells it how to call the Scenario server, and to price each call first.
An expert skill ships scripts that the agent runs inside Blender, Maya or an engine.

left.title: The post
left.say: The post says six departments and eighty skills.

right.title: The repo
right.say: The repo has one hundred sixty-seven skills in two tiers, and no folder named for a department.

scenes.label: cloud skills call model_run, the paid generation tool
scenes.say: Seventy-two of the eighty cloud skills call the paid generation tool, so most of them need a Scenario account.

scenes.label: expert skills sit just under the 2,500-word cap
scenes.note: the style check fails any longer body
scenes.say: Fifty-three of the eighty-seven expert skills sit just under the twenty-five hundred word cap. A cap shapes what gets written.

scenes.text: Count the files before you trust the headline. The strong part is the 87 expert skills, not the 80.
scenes.say: Count the files before you trust the headline. The strongest part is the expert tier, not the eighty.
Eighty cloud skills, eighty-seven expert skills, and departments that exist only in the post.
